A person who has hacked your computer and can see the reading pane can already has access your data. Removing the reading pane adds no security.

But if you feel better, F8 key toggles it, but does not remove it. Or View > Layout > Message Pane
creator: wsmwk

content:
See the menu option <View | Layout | Message Pane> or press <F8> to toggle it between hidden and not. If the Menu Bar is hidden, press <Alt> or <F8> to reveal it.

But I think your concern is misplaced. For one, how are you going to read the message without the message pane? For another, if someone has control of your computer, they will be able to get to data one way or another.

If this is a big concern for you, you should consider using disk encryption and password protecting the computer itself.

content:
There have been major ongoing problems with Spectrum/Charter/TWC/Roadrunner lately. Neither mail.twc.com (TWC's email servers) or mobile.charter.net (Spectrum and Charter's servers) appear to be online right now and may have been down for some time. From what we hear from their users, service has been intermittent for a while but it's gotten worse in the past week or few. It is not specifically a Thunderbird issue - it appears to affect most or all 3rd-party email clients, including Outlook, eMClient, Blue Mail, etc. Spectrum's support usually (but not always!) won't admit to any problems, but has explicitly stated that they only support webmail.

Here's a link to Spectrum's own user forum where you can see many discussions of the situation:

https://community.spectrum.net/categories/email-22

If you have time and patience you could contact Spectrum for status.

I have seen mention of a possible temporary workaround, which is to change the SMTP server to "mail.brighthouse.com". I can't verify that this works, or if it does that it won't quit working at any time, but it's easy enough to try and you can change it back to the existing name if it's not effective.

Otherwise, until they fix their servers your only recourse for now is to use their webmail. Or consider finding another, more reliable email provider.
